ety.text: Cognate with Old Church Slavonic юсеница (jusenica), Ukrainian гу́сениця (húsenycja), Bulgarian гъсе́ница (găsénica), Serbo-Croatian гу̏сеница/gȕsenica/гу̏сјеница/gȕsjenica, Slovene gosẹ̑nica, Czech housenka, Slovak húsenica, Old Polish wąsienica, Polish gąsienica, Upper Sorbian husańca, Lower Sorbian guseńca. Probably from Proto-Slavic *ǫsěnica. The initial г- (g-) is prothetic or by conflation with Common Slavonic гоущерица (gušterica, “lizard”) (Russian я́щерица (jáščerica)), and is not related to гусь (gusʹ, “goose”).
